question: Nitin has ₹1617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Pravin and Rishi and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Pravin and Rishi got same amount after 17 and 18 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Nitin give to Pravin?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When compound interest amounts are equal, the Ratio of Principals = (1 + R/100)Time Differeⁿce.

The principal invested for the shorter time will be proportionally larger.

Ratio of Pravin's share to Rishi's share = (1 + 10/100)¹⁸ − ¹⁷ : 1 = 11 : 10.

Total parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts → ₹1617.

Pravin's share (11 parts) = (1617 ÷ 21) × 11 = 77 × 11 = ₹847.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount received by Pravin = Amount received by Rishi

⇒ Pravin's Share × (1 + 10/100)¹⁷ = Rishi's Share × (1 + 10/100)¹⁸

⇒ Pravin's Share / Rishi's Share = (11/10)¹⁸ / (11/10)¹⁷

⇒ Pravin's Share / Rishi's Share = (11/10)¹⁸ − ¹⁷ = 11 / 10

⇒ Ratio of Pravin's share to Rishi's share = 11 : 10

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21

⇒ 21 parts = ₹1617

⇒ 1 part = 1617 ÷ 21 = ₹77

⇒ Pravin's share = 11 parts = 11 × 77 = ₹847

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

Compound interest is calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Splitting Sum into Equal CI Amounts

When a total sum is split into two parts P₁ and P₂ such that they yield equal amounts after T₁ and T₂ years, their ratio directly depends on the time gap: P₁ : P₂ = (1 + R/100)T² − T¹.

SI vs CI Difference for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 years on a certain sum is consistently calculated using the formula D = P(R/100)².
